boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Darbytown & New Market Roads record (October 7, 1864) in the Richmond-Petersburg Campaign [June 1864-March 1865]. Chaffin's Farm (VA075) precedes on September 29-30 and the Darbytown Road reconnaissance (VA078) follows on October 13. Army-wide returns, raid-wide and multi-action loss totals, and the siege as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Humphreys says Kautz was routed with the loss of eight guns but Field's attack on the Tenth Corps was repulsed; Lee says the enemy was driven to the New Market road, where he was not dislodged, and that guns, caissons, colors, horses and prisoners were taken.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The rout of the cavalry and the repulse at the main line are both retained.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,750 total and the live field 1,158 (US 458; CS 700). Humphreys gives Kautz's loss as eight guns, 72 killed and wounded and 202 missing, and names Gregg killed and Bratton wounded; Lee's dispatch said his loss was small and the enemy's unknown, and his correction gives 10 caissons, 2 colors, about 100 horses and over 100 prisoners (the gun count reads '0' in OCR).
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Kautz's and Birney's reports (Volume XLII No. 335; Birney No. 250 covers other dates), the Tenth Corps brigade reports, Field's, Hoke's and Longstreet's reports and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, later commander of its Second Corps, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; it relies on Meade's, Hancock's, Warren's, Burnside's, Parke's and Wilson's reports and quotes Lee's, Beauregard's and Gordon's despatches, so it is not independent of those families. Gillmore's, Meade's, Hancock's, Burnside's, Wilson's, Hampton's, Stannard's and Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXVI (Part 2), XL, XLII and XLVI (Part 1), are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; each volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Lee's telegrams largely relay subordinates' reports. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
